subject: Launch carveout & seasonal smoothing for monthly commit tiers

Cc: Procurement Team <procurement@oriongames.com>

Subject: SOW + launch month spike — need carveout/credits

Markus,

Thanks for the demo yesterday — Orion's product launch is scheduled for the first week of July and we expect a large short-term spike in API usage tied to onboarding early users (roughly a 2.5–3x uplift for ~10 days). We're interested in the monthly commit + per-token pricing you quoted, but procurement/legal want explicit language for a short-term launch carveout so we don't get hit with heavy overage charges for a predictable launch burst.

Attached is our draft SOW and a simple forecast (Week 1: ~1.2B tokens, baseline 400M/month afterward). Two quick asks:
- Can Redwood provide a one-time launch credit or temporary spike buffer for July?
- Alternatively, can we structure a step-up commit that ramps baseline over 2 months with a smoothing/true-up?

Would appreciate an outline of options and how credits vs. step-ups would be reflected on the invoice and against committed minimums.

Thanks — looping in our legal lead Sarah (cc).

— James
VP Product, Orion Games

Subject: Re: SOW + launch month spike — need carveout/credits

James — thanks for the SOW and context. Monica (AM) and Ben (finance) are copied to help scope commercial options. High-level options we typically offer for launch spikes:

1) One-time Launch Credit: a fixed invoice credit applied after the month to offset tokens above baseline. Does not reduce the committed minimum. Works well when the spike is timeboxed.

2) Graduated Step-up Commit: agree a month-by-month commit increase (e.g., 400M -> 700M -> 900M) with tiered per-token discounts. True-up can be spread over a 30–90 day window to avoid one-off invoice shocks.

3) Surge Protection Cap: cap per-token overage rate for a defined burst window (e.g., first 14 days of launch) and bill at a negotiated reduced overage rate beyond baseline.

Attached: a short playbook with clause snippets and a sample carveout calculation (Redwood_Launch_Carveout_Playbook.pdf). Can you confirm:
- expected daily shape during the 10-day spike (avg tokens/day)
- whether Orion requires the credit to apply against the committed minimum or only as an invoice credit

If you prefer, Monica can send a concrete quote with both options (credits vs. step-up) for your procurement/legal review.

Best,
Markus Klein
Head of Sales, Redwood Inference
Attachment: Redwood_Launch_Carveout_Playbook.pdf

Hi James — following up with an example we typically propose when a customer has a known launch window. I redlined a couple of terms on your SOW (attached) and sketched a numbers example so procurement can see the math quickly.

Example (illustrative):
- Agreed baseline commit (monthly): 500M tokens
- Projected July peak: 1.5B tokens (10-day concentrated spike)
- Option A (Launch Credit): One-time invoice credit equal to 25% of tokens above baseline up to the first 1B excess (i.e., credit applies to the first 1B above baseline). Credit applied as invoice credit on July invoice, not applied to committed minimum.
- Option B (Step-up): 500M (Jun) -> 800M (Jul) -> 1.0B (Aug) with tiered per-token price breaks; 60-day true-up so overages in July are amortized into Aug/Sep billing to smooth cashflow.

Notes:
- Credit vs. committed minimum: procurement often prefers credits as they preserve committed numbers for volume discounting; legal prefers simple credit language whereas finance prefers amortized true-ups.
- We can include a 30-day grace period for token accounting adjustments during launch month.

Attachment: redlined_terms_v2.docx (docx, 65KB) — includes a sample carveout clause and the specific invoice-credit language.

If this looks good, I can generate the formal quote and DocuSign envelope. Ben — are these parameters acceptable from a billing/finance perspective?

Thanks,
Monica
Account Manager, Redwood Inference

Monica — this is helpful, thank you. A couple clarifications from procurement/legal: 
1) Will the launch credit be reflected as a line-item credit on the invoice (preferred) or as a reduction to the per-token price for July (less preferred)?
2) If we take Option B (Step-up), can we set a lower minimum for June (300M) while still keeping the Jul->Aug ramp? That helps our cash management before launch.

Also, legal asks whether the credit cap can be limited to the first 1B excess tokens (you suggested that in the example) and to explicitly state that credits do not reduce committed minimums. If you can send an updated quote with both options and the language we can send to Legal, we can expedite. We'll need a DocuSign link + PO once agreed.

James — thanks. Final commercial proposal below; I included both options so procurement/legal can pick the mechanism they prefer. I've attached the formal quote and populated a DocuSign envelope for signature.

Final proposal (summary):
- Baseline commit: 300M tokens (June), ramp to 700M (July), 1.0B (Aug onward) as committed months.
- Per-token pricing: tiered; base tier for 0–300M at $0.000012/token, 300M–1B at $0.000009/token, >1B at $0.0000075/token (see attached quote for full bands).
- Launch Carveout Option A (Invoice Credit): One-time invoice credit equal to 25% of tokens above baseline for up to 1B excess tokens during July. Credit appears as a line-item on the July invoice and does NOT reduce the committed minimum.
- Launch Carveout Option B (Step-up + True-up): Commit schedule 300M -> 700M -> 1.0B with a 60-day true-up: any overage in July is amortized into Aug/Sep invoices to smooth charges. Step-up preserves tiered pricing and counts toward committed usage.
- Surge Protection: For the 14-day launch window, capped overage price of $0.0000095/token for tokens above 1B (if hit).
- PO & Billing: Credit can be applied as invoice credit. We require a PO for the committed billing term; credits don't offset the PO value.

Attachments: Final_Quote_ORION-2027-001.pdf (pdf), DocuSign envelope: https://docusign.net/envelope/ABC12345

If this matches what you need, I'll route the DocuSign for signature and Ben will kick off billing setup.
